posts.author: MDR
posts.body:
Fair point.
I changed the title of the thread. Here's the example.
I have a cutscene where a roof of a burning building collapses on itself half way through the scene. Instead of using events and switches in RMMZ, I decided to do the tile swap using levels in Tiled. It seemed cleaner.
I created two layers Before Roof Collapsed and Roof Collapsed, and gave them the correct priorities that display and disappear each layer depending on the level the player is on. During the cutscene I use Set Movement Route to move the player over toLvl1 collision tile. In theory this should swap the roof tiles, but it doesn't. To test whether it's an issue with the Set Movement Route or Tiled, I restored full movement at the end of the cutscene, moved the player off the toLvl1 tile and back onto it, and the tiles swapped like they should.
Conclusion: it doesn't seem like Set Movement Route command can be used to trigger a to-Lvl tile collision.

posts.author: Solar_Flare

Click to expand...
Well, it normally doesn't show up by default, but I think VisuStella might change that so it does. You can also access it by pressing F8.
Is the swap directly triggered by an event or is it something that's automatically handled somehow? If it's the former, you could try
this.checkEventTriggerHere([1,2])
as a move route script. But, triggering an event while another (non-parallel) event is running probably isn't really supported. It would be better to take the thing you're doing in the event and do the exact same thing in a move route script.

posts.author: MDR
posts.body:
debugger language is not something I’m good at so I’ll try to explain the best I can. Apologies if I’m explaining something you already know.
The tile swap isn’t triggered within the event, rather a player’s movement over a tile with level properties assigned in Tiled. The most common example of its use is showing a bridge above and below a player pending what level they are on. You make two tile layers of the same bridge in Tiled, one layered above the player the other layered below. Depending on what level the player is on, one layer is visible while the other is invisible. The swap is triggered when a player walks over a tile with a level property (eg toLvl0, toLvl1).
However, I think there’s a restriction to how the player steps on the level tile. You cannot activate a level tile by teleporting a player onto it. I think the same is true for Set Movement Route. The player has to walk over the level tile using the mouse or direction keys.
Anyways, I opted for a more interactive approach to this cutscene. The player is forced to follow another character and in the process walk over the level tile and triggering the tile swap and roof collapse. It actually flows nicer for the player.
Thanks again SF

For continuity of good advice. I actually found a simple solution in the Visustella Tiled sample project. It was right in front of me and didn't notice.
I believe it is map4 that outlines how Levels work in tiled, there's a pro tip that states:
This plugin comes with a simple command you can us in MZ. (Event command/Plugin Command/VisuMZ_5_TiledMZ/) called Set Map Level.
Simply input the level you want to change to manually, but this is a cumbersome way to do it, recommended only for special occasions like cutscenes and similar non-exploration.
In case someone else is reading this thread, I wanted them to have this solution.

posts.body:
Solar_Flare said:
By default you would do this by putting a
!
at the beginning of the spritesheet's filename.
Click to expand...
So here's the problem with doing it that way.
When using Tiled, if you:
place a ! at the beginning of the spritesheet's filename and;
use that spritesheet in an event with the priority set to Below character
The event isn't visible because it gets drops below all the Tiled layers.
But as you stated in another thread, you can simple use a script command (this._priorityType = 2) in the movement route.
